Business goal: Create a durable planning record for a new governed frontend page shell.
User outcome: A root operator can start a new page-shell plan with selected hierarchy location, template family, route, nav posture, and allowed roles.
Notes / constraints: This first slice is planning-only and must not ask template-specific mapping questions. The accepted client shape is limited to page-shell fields only. Canonical design-system source, shell context, secondary-nav group, and secondary-nav icon are derived server-side, and system-managed lifecycle fields are never client-supplied. Repo-derived catalogs should come from synchronized planner-facing read models rather than hand-maintained planner data.
Tenant context rule: root-operated planning capability outside tenant-scoped authorization; no tenant context applies
Explicitly denied roles: tenant actors; unauthenticated callers; authenticated root users without the governing capability
Authorization summary: Only privileged root operators may create page-shell planning records. The capability is root-only and must not silently widen into general app-user planning access.
Authz scope type: exact create over one new plan
Frontend visibility rule: No frontend surface is required in v1 because the first slice is backend and export focused.
Backend enforcement rule: Root auth and root authorization must run before plan creation. Validate selected hierarchy, feature area, template family, nav posture, and allowed roles against current catalog truth. Reject client-supplied derived or system-managed fields.
Session / expiry behavior: Uses existing authenticated root-session expiry rules. No tenant session behavior applies.
Request contract: Body includes pageId, pageName, pageHierarchyId, featureArea, route, pagePurpose, templateFamilyId, optional secondaryNavLabel, allowedRoleKeys, and optional notes.
Response contract: Returns created plan detail with pageShellPlanId, pageId, pageName, pageHierarchyId, featureArea, route, shellContext, pagePurpose, templateFamilyId, derived secondaryNavGroup, optional secondaryNavLabel, derived secondaryNavIcon, allowedRoleKeys, derived canonicalDesignSystemSource, status=draft, createdAt, updatedAt, exportedAt=null, supersededAt=null, and notes.
Error contract: 400 invalid payload or incompatible catalog selections, including rejected system-managed or derived fields; 401 unauthenticated; 403 unauthorized; 404 referenced hierarchy, feature area, template family, or role not found; 409 duplicate pageId or route collision.
Cross-feature seams: Depends on explicit planner catalog capabilities for selectable values and the existing root-roles seam for allowed role truth. Secondary-nav group and icon derive from hierarchy and shell posture rather than their own planner inputs.
Persistence impact: Insert one durable page-shell plan row plus normalized allowed-role junction rows.
Indexes / uniqueness: Unique index on pageId. Unique active index on route within shellContext. Validated references for pageHierarchyId, featureArea, templateFamily, and related nav catalogs. Index on status and updatedAt for operator review.
Search / filter model: Exact create only; no search surface in this capability.
Compatibility / migration notes: Model should remain compatible with a later frontend wizard and later template-specific planning seams without changing the durable page-shell identity or export shape.
Authorization enforcement layer: Root auth middleware plus root authorization enforcement and feature-local catalog validation.
CSP / browser security impact: No direct browser impact in API-only v1. Future same-origin planning UI must reuse the governed form-template posture and approved child seams only.
Audit requirement: Audit successful creates and denied attempts with actor rootUserId, plan identifiers, selected template family, route, and selected role metadata.
Privacy / personal data impact: Moderate; stores internal planning metadata and role visibility decisions but no end-user personal data in the first slice.
Standards impact: ASVS authorization and input-validation relevance. Standards review is useful because this introduces a new planning seam and durable export workflow.
Acceptance notes: Capability is acceptable when a privileged root operator can create one durable page-shell plan from accepted page-shell fields only, with validated catalogs, derived canonical source, derived nav posture metadata, normalized allowed roles, and no template-specific mapping inputs.

Business goal: Allow privileged operators to revise an existing page-shell plan before it is exported or superseded.
User outcome: A root operator can change page-shell planning fields without recreating the plan from scratch.
Notes / constraints: Updates must revalidate all changed catalog references and allowed roles against current truth. Derived canonicalDesignSystemSource, shellContext, secondaryNavGroup, and secondaryNavIcon remain server-managed. Update may only mutate accepted page-shell fields. Exported status remains owned by the export capability, not by general update. Normal update rules exclude superseded plans unless a later explicit restore or reopen capability is added.
Tenant context rule: root-operated planning capability outside tenant-scoped authorization; no tenant context applies
Explicitly denied roles: tenant actors; unauthenticated callers; authenticated root users without the governing capability
Authorization summary: Only privileged root operators may update page-shell planning records. Updates remain root-only and server-authoritative.
Frontend visibility rule: No frontend surface is required in v1 because the first slice is backend and export focused.
Backend enforcement rule: Root auth and root authorization must run before update. Feature validation must reject changes that break hierarchy or feature compatibility, route uniqueness, template sign-off, nav rules, or allowed role validity. Successful updates must refresh updatedAt.
Session / expiry behavior: Uses existing authenticated root-session expiry rules. No tenant session behavior applies.
Request contract: Exact pageShellPlanId param required. Body may include pageName, pageHierarchyId, featureArea, route, pagePurpose, templateFamilyId, optional secondaryNavLabel, allowedRoleKeys, notes, and allowed lifecycle transitions among draft, ready_for_export, and superseded.
Response contract: Returns updated plan detail with the same shape as exact read, refreshed updatedAt, and newly derived canonical or nav fields when the selected template or hierarchy changes.
Error contract: 400 invalid payload or incompatible catalog selections, including rejected system-managed fields; 401 unauthenticated; 403 unauthorized; 404 plan not found; 409 duplicate pageId, route collision, or invalid lifecycle transition.
Cross-feature seams: Depends on explicit planner catalog capabilities for selectable values and the existing root-roles seam for allowed role truth. Secondary-nav group and icon derive from hierarchy and shell posture rather than their own planner inputs.
Persistence impact: Update one durable page-shell plan row and replace or reconcile normalized allowed-role junction rows.
Indexes / uniqueness: Maintain unique pageId and route-within-shell guarantees. Index by status, updatedAt, and featureArea remains useful for operator review.
Search / filter model: Exact update only; no search surface in this capability.
Compatibility / migration notes: Keep update semantics compatible with later draft review workflows and export handoff without forcing consumers to recreate plans when a signed-off template or hierarchy decision changes.
Authorization enforcement layer: Root auth middleware plus root authorization enforcement and feature-local exact-plan validation.
CSP / browser security impact: No direct browser impact in API-only v1.
Audit requirement: Audit successful updates and denied attempts with before-and-after summaries for changed planning fields and role selections.
Privacy / personal data impact: Moderate; stores internal planning metadata and role visibility decisions but no end-user personal data in the first slice.
Standards impact: ASVS authorization and input-validation relevance. Standards review is useful because this capability mutates durable planning records and export-relevant truth.
Acceptance notes: Capability is acceptable when a privileged root operator can safely revise accepted page-shell fields only, while derived values, lifecycle ownership, and validation rules remain server-authoritative.

Business goal: Allow exact inspection of one saved page-shell plan.
User outcome: A root operator can retrieve one page-shell plan and review its current values, derived fields, allowed roles, and lifecycle state.
Notes / constraints: Normal reads should exclude superseded records unless a later explicit historical-read capability is added. Exact read is planning-detail only and must not imply export readiness by itself.
Tenant context rule: root-operated planning capability outside tenant-scoped authorization; no tenant context applies
Explicitly denied roles: tenant actors; unauthenticated callers; authenticated root users without the governing capability

Backend enforcement rule: Root auth and root authorization must run before read. Feature must resolve exactly one visible plan and return derived canonicalDesignSystemSource and normalized allowedRoleKeys from server truth.
Session / expiry behavior: Uses existing authenticated root-session expiry rules. No tenant session behavior applies.
Request contract: Exact pageShellPlanId param required. No body.
Response contract: Returns one page-shell plan with pageShellPlanId, pageId, pageName, pageHierarchyId, featureArea, route, shellContext, pagePurpose, templateFamilyId, derived secondaryNavGroup, optional secondaryNavLabel, derived secondaryNavIcon, allowedRoleKeys, derived canonicalDesignSystemSource, status, createdAt, updatedAt, exportedAt, supersededAt, and notes.
Error contract: 400 invalid identifier; 401 unauthenticated; 403 unauthorized; 404 plan not found or not normally visible.
Cross-feature seams: Depends on planner catalog read models only indirectly through derived display values and on normalized role associations.
Persistence impact: Read one durable page-shell plan row and its related role junction rows. No mutation.
Indexes / uniqueness: Primary key on pageShellPlanId plus supporting visibility rules over status or supersededAt.
Search / filter model: Exact read only; no search surface in this capability.
Compatibility / migration notes: Read contract should stay stable when later planner UIs or export tools consume the same plan detail record.
Authorization enforcement layer: Root auth middleware plus root authorization enforcement and feature-local exact-plan visibility rules.
CSP / browser security impact: No direct browser impact in API-only v1.
Audit requirement: Audit denied reads and add successful-read auditing only if the planner surface becomes compliance-sensitive later.
Privacy / personal data impact: Low to moderate; exposes internal planning and visibility metadata only to privileged root operators.
Standards impact: ASVS authorization relevance only; limited privacy impact because planning data is internal and non-personal in the initial slice.
Acceptance notes: Capability is acceptable when a privileged root operator can read one plan exactly and the response includes normalized roles and derived canonical source without exposing hidden internal-only fields.

Notes / constraints: List semantics should follow repo pagination defaults. V1 should stay narrow: status and featureArea filtering are enough for the first draft, and broad free-text search should not be implied unless it is explicitly specified and indexed later. Normal list visibility should exclude superseded records by default.

Compatibility / migration notes: Keep the list contract stable enough for a later planner list UI and CSV export picker without forcing a route or response redesign.
Authorization enforcement layer: Root auth middleware plus root authorization enforcement and feature-local pagination validation.
CSP / browser security impact: No direct browser impact in API-only v1.
Audit requirement: Audit denied list attempts. Successful list auditing is optional unless planner visibility becomes sensitive later.
Privacy / personal data impact: Low to moderate; exposes internal planning metadata only to privileged root operators.
Standards impact: ASVS authorization relevance with minimal privacy impact in the initial slice.
Acceptance notes: Capability is acceptable when a privileged root operator can list draft, ready_for_export, and exported plans with stable pagination and honest lifecycle visibility defaults.

Business goal: Produce the deterministic CSV artifact consumed by Codex and the downstream frontend implementation loop.
User outcome: A root operator can export one or more ready page-shell plans into stable new-page-shell-matrix.csv rows for repo review and commit.
Notes / constraints: Export must be deterministic and must not include template-specific mapping data. Only plans in ready_for_export or exported status should be exportable in the first slice. allowedRoleKeys must be sorted and pipe-delimited in stable order. Export owns the transition into exported state and the stamping of exportedAt.
Tenant context rule: root-operated planning capability outside tenant-scoped authorization; no tenant context applies
Explicitly denied roles: tenant actors; unauthenticated callers; authenticated root users without the governing capability

Request contract: Request identifies selected pageShellPlanIds or an explicitly approved export scope. Only plans in exportable lifecycle states are accepted.

CSP / browser security impact: No direct browser impact in API-only v1. Future same-origin export UI must still remain within the governed form and shell posture.
Audit requirement: Audit successful exports and denied export attempts with actor rootUserId, selected plan ids, output filename or scope, and resulting lifecycle changes.
Privacy / personal data impact: Low to moderate; exports internal planning and visibility metadata for repo review but no end-user personal data in the first slice.
Standards impact: ASVS authorization and integrity relevance. Standards and repo-health review matter because this capability produces anti-drift source artifacts consumed by Codex and future implementation loops.
Acceptance notes: Capability is acceptable when a privileged root operator can export stable new-page-shell-matrix rows from validated plans only, with deterministic ordering, server-derived canonical fields, derived nav posture metadata, and export-owned lifecycle stamping.
